rules.cwe_name: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
rules.description: Sensitive cookies set by a server can be read by the client if the `httpOnly` flag is not set.

rules.cwe_name: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
rules.description: DOM functions that act like 'eval' and execute strings as code are dangerous and impede program analysis and understanding. Consequently, they should not be used.

rules.cwe_name: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source
rules.description: Including functionality from an untrusted source may allow an attacker to control the functionality and execute arbitrary code.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
rules.description: Untrusted CR or LF characters are not neutralized before use in line-delimited protocol metadata.

rules.cwe_name: Assignment to Variable without Use
rules.description: If two functions with the same name are declared in the same scope, one of the declarations overrides the other without warning. This makes the code hard to read and maintain, and may even lead to platform-dependent behavior.

rules.cwe_name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in a Cookie
rules.description: Sensitive information stored without encryption or hashing can expose it to an attacker.

rules.cwe_name: Modification of Assumed-Immutable Data (MAID)
rules.description: Security-critical data assumed immutable can be modified by an attacker.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Client-side URL redirection based on unvalidated user input may cause redirection to malicious web sites.

rules.cwe_name: Credentials Management Errors
rules.description: Legacy category for insecure credential creation, storage, validation, or handling.

rules.cwe_name: Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers
rules.description: Tokens used for sensitive tasks, such as, password recovery, and email confirmation, should not use predictable values.
